column23:
1. 1. Clear the field and Tab. Separately, clear the field, type abc, and Tab.
  2. 2. "Expected (measured live, with a passing control alongside)": both render "0%", validation error is
  3. 3. "false", "Update stays enabled", and no message appears.
  4. 4. | Trial | Before | After blur | validation error | Update |
  5. 5. |---|---|---|---|---|
  6. 6. | cleared | 17% | "0%" | false | "enabled" |
  7. 7. | abc | 17% | "0%" | false | "enabled" |
  8. 8. | 14 (control) | 17% | 14% | false | enabled |
  9. 9. "This case previously read "both leave the field empty with is invalid and Update disabled.""
  10. 10. That came from a single unreplicated walk observation and is "refuted": the field is not rejecting
  11. 11. anything, it is substituting zero. The control trial passed in the same run, so the harness is not in
  12. 12. question.
  13. 13. "Status": asserts "observed" behaviour, not agreed-correct behaviour. A user who mistypes into a
  14. 14. percentage field gets a silent 0% with Save still available, so an unintended zero discount can be
  15. 15. committed with no warning. Note the criteria-bar threshold field "reverts to its previous value" for
  16. 16. the same input - see TC-039 - so two fields of the same class on one screen disagree

column23:
1. 1. Record the threshold. Type a different valid value, Tab, and - "without saving" - click the
  2. 2. Region Weekly Peaks tab, then return to Company Matrix. Then reload the route.
  3. 3. "Expected (measured live)":
  4. 4. - After the tab round trip -> the typed value is "still there". No Unsaved-Changes prompt appears on
  5. 5. the way out or back.
  6. 6. - After the reload -> the threshold is back to its original value. Nothing was persisted.
  7. 7. "This case previously expected the tab switch itself to discard the edit." It does not. The threshold
  8. 8. lives in the page-level criteria bar, "outside" every tab panel - the same reason the Save button is a
  9. 9. page header control - so switching tabs never unmounts it. The earlier "the value is gone" reading was
  10. 10. taken after a "fresh navigation", not after switching back, and the two were conflated.
  11. 11. "Status": asserts "observed" behaviour, not agreed-correct behaviour. A reported reproduction implies a prompt should exist here and none does
  12. 12. whether that absence is intentional or a regression is
  13. 13. unresolved. A user can leave a pending edit on screen, wander to another tab and come back with no
  14. 14. indication anything is unsaved. Treat a future prompt as a change worth reporting, not a failure.
  15. 15. "Status": this asserts "observed" behaviour, not agreed-correct behaviour. A reported reproduction implies a prompt should exist here. Whether its absence is an intentional change or a regression is unresolved -
  16. 16. see the walk evidence. Treat a future appearance of a prompt as a change worth reporting, not a failure
